sections.h2: What kind of place is Arlington Heights for a home seller?
sections.html:
Arlington Heights lies in Cook County roughly 25 miles northwest of the Loop, and a sliver of the village reaches into Lake County. Its 16.61 square miles are almost entirely developed, so a seller here competes with other established blocks.

The 2020 count was 77,676 people, the 15th largest municipality in the state. The July 2025 Census estimate of 76,216 sits 1.9% under that base, and one resident in five is 65 or older.

The village's history page calls the downtown Metra station the anchor of a walkable district of shops, restaurants and entertainment.

sections.h2: How did Arlington Heights grow, and why does that matter for an older house?
sections.html:
The settlement started as Dunton, a depot stop, and took the name Arlington Heights in 1874. Farms and greenhouses covered most of the ground into the postwar years.

Then came the 1950s and 1960s. Automobiles, the baby boom and a string of annexations lifted the count to 64,884 by 1970, by which time nearly all open land was gone. A house from those decades draws close attention from inspectors at the roof deck, the electrical panel, the supply piping and the basement walls.

  • Request the village permit file for your address.
  • Collect paperwork showing when the furnace, water heater and roof were replaced.
  • Find out whether a finished lower level or an addition went through permitting when it was built.

sections.h2: What do parks and local landmarks add to a listing?
sections.html:
The Arlington Heights Park District owns 456.53 acres and leases another 258.56 acres across 58 parks. Lake Arlington, a human-made 50-acre detention lake, sits inside a 93-acre park with a 1.8-mile path around the water, and the district also runs pools, courts, golf courses and a senior center.

Downtown has the Metropolis Performing Arts Centre, which opened in 1999, and the Arlington Heights Memorial Library, where 63.5 percent of residents held cards in 2014. Mitsuwa Marketplace, the largest Japanese supermarket in the Midwest, is in the village. Frontier Days at Recreation Park, held before Independence Day, draws a carnival and a parade.

Mention whatever is closest to your house, since a short walk to a park or the station is the kind of detail a buyer remembers.

sections.h2: What does the local economy look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2022 figures put retail sales in Arlington Heights at $1.67 billion, health care and social assistance receipts at $1.57 billion, and accommodation and food service sales at $221 million. Retail works out to $22,237 per resident, well above the figure for Aurora or Batavia.

About two thirds of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and 60.4% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The share of residents born abroad is 21.5%, and 28.8% of residents speak a language other than English at home.

sections.h2: What is going on with the Arlington Park property?
sections.html:
The former racetrack at 3200 W. Euclid Ave. covers 326 acres, and the Chicago Bears Football Club bought it in February 2023. The village keeps a redevelopment page for it, and that page carries a statement that the team announced it would focus on a stadium opportunity in Indiana.

The village adds that it still regards the property as a highly viable redevelopment site because of its size, transportation access and place in the northwest suburbs. For a seller nearby, the future use of that land is unsettled. Buyers will ask what you know, so read the current village page and answer from it.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Arlington Heights homes?
sections.html:
Elementary and middle students in most of the village attend Arlington Heights School District 25, and District 214 runs the high schools. Parts of the village belong instead to Districts 15, 21, 23, 57 or 59, which means two neighbors can have different schools.

  • South Middle School and Thomas Middle School are District 25 schools.
  • John Hersey High School is the only public high school inside village limits; some areas feed Buffalo Grove, Prospect, Rolling Meadows or Wheeling, and a few feed Palatine High School in District 211.

Verify the assignment for the exact street before writing it into a listing.

sections.h2: Can a buyer use the house as a short-term rental in Arlington Heights?
sections.html:
Not for stays under 30 consecutive days. The Village Board's March 2, 2026 ordinance set a 30-day minimum on all residential rentals, effective July 1, 2026, and it did not grandfather existing short-term rentals. Shorter stays count as nuisances, and the village acts on complaints.

Hotels, motels and lodging rooms are exempt. Sellers get a carve-out: if the rental agreement is signed along with the contract to sell, a seller may stay on after closing for fewer than 30 consecutive days. Ask the closing attorney to draft it that way.

sections.h2: What do permits and building codes mean when you sell?
sections.html:
Permits run through the Building & Life Safety Department and its online Civic Access Portal, where applicants can track a permit, book inspections and upload documents. The counter is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, with a 9:30 a.m. start on the first and third Wednesday, and the phone is 847-368-5560.

Work may take place between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. on weekdays and between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekends. The village has adopted the 2024 International codes, replacing 2018 editions, with an effective date of January 1, 2027, and the department tells applicants to read the updated requirements before submitting.

sections.h2: How are the deed and transfer tax handled on an Arlington Heights sale?
sections.html:
State transfer tax is paid with revenue stamps bought through the county recorder. Both sides sign the PTAX-203 declaration, filed where the parcel is. Whether a county or home rule municipality adds a charge of its own is a question for the title company.

In Cook County, the Clerk's schedule prices a deed at $107, a total that bundles recording, GIS, storage, state housing and filer fees, and that schedule has applied since April 1, 2024. The Lake County slice of the village records with that county.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for an Arlington Heights house?
sections.html:
Cash works when the roof or kitchen is dated, when an estate or divorce sets the clock, or when months of showings and loan approvals are not an option. The trade is simple: speed and certainty in exchange for the price a fully updated listing might reach.

  • Line up any offer against what a listing would put in your pocket after agent fees and repairs.
  • Ask who covers the title search and recording, and get it in the contract.
  • Confirm the day of closing, plus what happens to utilities and your belongings that day.

A signed purchase agreement, a title commitment and a clear closing statement protect you on either route.

faqs.q: How fast can an Arlington Heights cash sale close?
faqs.a: It can close on whatever date the contract names, since no lender has to approve anything. Recording in Cook County runs through the County Clerk, so give the title company time to prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Must I repair the house first?
faqs.a: No, but open permits deserve attention. Pull the record from Building & Life Safety and finalize anything unfinished. Cosmetic work is optional when you sell as-is.

faqs.q: Can I stay in the house after closing?
faqs.a: Yes, for a short time. The village lets a buyer and seller sign a rental agreement of under 30 consecutive days if it is executed together with the contract to sell. Without that paper, short stays at a residential rental are treated as nuisances.

faqs.q: Who writes the check for transfer taxes?
faqs.a: Whatever the contract says, so read that clause. Your title company can itemize each tax and name the party responsible.

faqs.q: Where does my deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the recorder for the parcel's county. That is the Cook County Clerk for most of the village and Lake County for the small piece there. Look up your parcel number to be sure.
